title: Impact of Reforms at Family Justice Courts
what_it_is: Impact of Reforms at Family Justice Courts

sections.label: Divorce judgment times reduced
sections.summary: Average time for Interim Judgment fell from 68.6 days in 2012 to 53.1 days in 2016, and Final Judgment from 155.3 to 114.6 days.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Ms Indranee Rajah) (for the Minister for Law)
sentences.text: The average time taken for divorce cases to be granted Interim Judgment has been reduced from 68.6 days in 2012 to 53.1 days in 2016.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Ms Indranee Rajah) (for the Minister for Law)
sentences.text: Similarly, the average time taken for Final Judgment to be granted has also been reduced from 155.3 days in 2012 to 114.6 days in 2016.

sections.label: New family justice committee
sections.summary: MinLaw, MSF and the Family Justice Courts decided to convene a new committee to further enhance the family justice system.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Ms Indranee Rajah) (for the Minister for Law)
sentences.text: In this regard, the Ministry of Law (MinLaw), MSF and the Family Justice Courts have decided to convene a new committee to further enhance the family justice system.

sections.label: Reforming family justice system
sections.summary: Reforms will continue through a less adversarial, more efficient, more child-centric approach and community support, as some Clementi residents were distressed by outcomes.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Ms Indranee Rajah) (for the Minister for Law)
sentences.text: We will continue to make reforms and improve our family justice system to better support and preserve families going through a dispute, through a less adversarial, more efficient and more child-centric approach to family litigation, as well as a robust network of community support.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: I say this because I have met residents in Clementi, some of whom did not attend these hearings and were subsequently distressed when the outcome went against them.

sections.label: Unrepresented persons requesting postponement
sections.summary: Those who cannot attend can write to the Court in advance, and the Court will usually consider valid reasons and accommodate them.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: For those who are not represented, if for some reason they truly cannot turn up to ask for an adjournment or postponement, they can, at the very minimum, write to the Court in advance of the hearing, and the Court will usually take into account whether or not the reasons for the request for the postponement are good reasons, and they will accommodate if the reasons are valid.

sections.label: Lawyers' role and accreditation
sections.summary: The role lawyers can play is why the Family Law Accreditation Scheme is being looked at.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: On the second question on what role can lawyers play, that is a very good question.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: That is the reason why we are looking at the Family Law Accreditation Scheme.

sections.label: Specialist training for family lawyers
sections.summary: Lawyers need specialist training to deal with family justice, which is considered very important.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: And the lawyer needs to be able to deal with that.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: So, it is for this reason that we consider it very important that lawyers have specialist training to deal with family justice.

sections.label: Family law and maintenance enforcement
sections.summary: Family law is important, and the Ministry tracks enforcement applications rather than compliance figures, though enforcement can be difficult when payers hide assets.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: In short, family law is not just a poor cousin to commercial law.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: It is a very important area of the law and the lawyers who practice it should become specialist lawyers in their own right.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
sentences.text: Does the Ministry keep track of whether these are adhered to and, if not, are there ways which we could make it less painful, make it more seamless for those who are supposed to receive the payments but are not receiving them?

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: We do not have the specific figures of which orders are complied with and which are not because, obviously, for the ones which are complied with, the parties will not come back to the Court.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: But you will know whether the rates of compliance are steady or going up or falling by the number of applications for enforcement with the Courts.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: We are able to track those, although I do not have the specific figures with me right now.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: That said, there are instances where enforcement is difficult and frustrating, particularly when the spouse who has to pay maintenance either hides assets or it is difficult to find.
